HODDER & STOUGHTON
About this book
Novels of suspense can be classified as
such under two headings: those which
depend simply on the reader's desire to
know
"who did it" and those which
create suspense through the imagination
by forcing the reader to shiver not in his
own shoes but in someone else's. It is
among the distinguished company under
this second heading that we must place
Eric Ambler's new thriller, " Journey
into Fear."
The time is now. The traveller is a
British engineer returning home from
a business trip to Istanbul: a man com-
fortably aware of his own security in a
world at war and believing that some
things couldn't possibly happen to him,
that " death could only come with the
sweet reason of disease or an • Act of
God.' "
And then he discovers that
death is
at
his
elbow, sudden
and
horrible death, " waiting to make non-
sense of all his comfortable ideas about
his relations with time and chance, ready
to remind him—in case he had forgotten
-that civilization was a word and that
he still lived in a jungle."
Those who already know Eric Ambler's
work will need no encouragement to get
this book.
The fact that it is a new
Ambler will be enough.
